History
At Hatchlands, it is our intention to provide all our children with a high-quality history education that will help pupils gain a coherent knowledge and understanding of Britain’s past and that of the wider world. We aspire for our pupils to be curious learners and have a thirst for knowledge about events beyond and within living memory. We intend for our pupils to develop the skills required to explore their own interests; asking questions, thinking critically, weighing evidence, and developing their own judgments. We want our pupils to understand how people’s lives and societies have changed over time, and how this has had an impact on their own identities.
changes of events within and beyond living memory that are significant nationally and globally
lives of significant individuals in the past who have contributed to national and international achievements.
significant historical events, people and places in their own locality
settlements and changes in Britain: Stone Age, Iron Age, Roman Empire, Vikings, Anglo-Saxons and Scots
achievements of early civilisations and non-European societies that contrasts with British History
evaluate and interpret a range of primary and secondary resources, and form reasoned conclusions
develop a strong sense of chronology through timelines, historical periods and have an overview of major events and figures.
make connections, contrasts and find trends over time
ask and answer questions using historical vocabulary

Spellings
Children in Years 2–6 will bring home a new spelling book to support their learning of spellings both in school and at home.
This book will help children keep all of their spelling lists in one place and provide a space for regular practice.
Each Monday, your child will stick their new spelling list into the book and use the next page to practise their spellings at home.
Spelling quizzes will then take place the following Monday, allowing plenty of time to practise in class and over the weekend.
To help you support your child at home, spelling lists for the whole term are available below

Headteachers Welcome
Welcome to Hatchlands Primary School
I am extremely proud to be the Headteacher of such an exciting, innovative and uniquely nurturing school. It is with confidence that I can say the children are at the heart of everything we do and our school is a place that is committed to inspiring children’s hearts and minds.
Our school motto is ‘Learning today, to make a difference tomorrow.'
As we all believe that instilling a love of learning and developing different learning skills is vital in preparing children for their future lives. We want our children to leave Hatchlands as confident and highly motivated, independent learners who are caring and positive citizens.
Our values of Compassion, Courage, Responsibility and Respect are an integral part of school life and support the ethos of our school. Wellbeing and achievement go hand in hand and a key priority for us as a school is that every child is happy both in and out of the classroom. We strongly believe that if a child is not happy, they will not thrive academically or socially. We work closely with parents to ensure that every individual’s needs are being met and that every child is confident and has positive self-esteem, as we believe happy children make good learners.
Our enthusiastic, professional and dedicated teaching team work hard to ensure that every child develops into an exceptional individual with a love for learning and the capacity to reach academic excellence.
We are committed to offering a vast range of opportunities at Hatchlands, both inside and outdoors, to light the spark of learning and equip your children with the skills and tools they need to take off and fly!
We hope our website provides you with the information you need, but please do not hesitate to contact us if we can provide any further information.

Writing
‘If you want to change the world, pick up a pen and write’ Martin Luther King
English lies at the heart of our curriculum with our book-based approach to writing. We are passionate about children having exposure to a wide breadth of rich literature that generates an interest in and love for writing, giving them access to the language, vocabulary and tools needed to write creatively and effectively. Through our engaging curriculum, we aspire to all pupils recognising themselves as writers who are confident in using written language to communicate for a range of audiences and purposes. Writing offers unique opportunities for children to learn about the world around them, discuss and debate their modern world and understand how we can learn from the positive characters demonstrated by the individuals they meet. By matching writing topics to our wider curriculum, children will have immediate opportunities to share their learning and reinforce links between subject content. We use Colourful Semantics to support all learners in writing by providing clear sentence structures that can be replicated.
Children will learn about:
A range of genres, identifying their purpose and relevance to the audience they are writing
A range of authors and how they manipulate language and structure to make their writing engaging
Writing as a way to convey and evoke emotions and feelings in others
Why writing is widely celebrated with the opportunity to celebrate their own work
Children will learn how:
To write for a range of purposes
We can communicate through various written forms
To write legibly in a cursive style
To apply a range of spelling patterns in their writing
To include a range of grammatical structures suitable to the purpose of their piece
To present their work in a range of different layouts
To edit and publish work, casting a critical eye over what they have written
